fields.name: Maṅgarāja Mahāpātra
fields.notes: An officer of King Pratāparudra; with Haricandana brought a new boat for Lord Caitanya at Cuttack on His way to Vṛndāvana and went with Him (CC Madhya 16.113-116). Perhaps two persons (Maṅgarāja and Mahāpātra) merged into one (Bhakti Movement in Orissa 86).

fields.works: Rāya Rāmānanda; Svarūpa Dāmodara; Caraṇa-tulasī; Vidyāpati; Caṇḍīdāsa; Sādhana-saṅketa; Śrī Rūpa-Sanātana; Śrī Vaiṣṇava; Śrī Nityānanda; Gambhīrāya Śrī Gaurāṅga; Nīlācale Vraja-mādhurī; Līlā-mādhurī; Gīta-govinda; Sānuvāda Sarva-saṁvādinī; Vaiṣṇava periodicals
fields.notes: Of the line of Śrīnivāsa Ācārya's second daughter (born 1848, Digdarśanī); lived more than a hundred years; learned in Eastern and Western studies; wrote many Vaiṣṇava books, edited Vaiṣṇava periodicals and expounded the śāstras. (The poet Rasikānanda of Padakalpataru 2227 has his own record since 11-11-2026.)

fields.place: Cātrā near Śrīrāmapura (Hooghly); Saibonā (24 Parganas: his descendants)
fields.guru: Kāśīnātha Paṇḍita of Cātarā = Kāśīśvara Paṇḍita (#1832), his uncle
fields.notes: Nephew and disciple of Kāśīnātha (Kāśīśvara) Paṇḍita of Cātarā (#1832), associate of Lord Gaurāṅga — not Kāśīnātha of Navadvīpa (#692); brother of Rudra Paṇḍita of Vallabhapura; married at Saibonā, where his descendants hold a festival in Māgha. Of the three Deities carved from one stone by Vīrabhadra (Śyāmasundara, Rādhāvallabha, Nandadulāla), the Nandadulāla of Saibonā — or, the Vaiṣṇavācāra-darpaṇa says, Madhu Paṇḍita installed it.
